steps.body: Circular motion IS a wave — watch a rider's HEIGHT. A wheel of radius 20 ft with its axle 25 ft up, boarding at the bottom, gives **h(t) = 25 − 20 cos t**: axle height as the midline, radius as the amplitude, and −cos because the ride STARTS at its lowest point.

dials.feedback: The wheel's radius is wrong. The amplitude is how far the rider swings above and below the centre.
The wheel is at the wrong height. The midline is the centre of the wheel above the ground.

widget.prompt: Build the Ferris wheel h(t) = 25 − 20 cos t with the dials, then read the rider's lowest point.
widget.successFeedback: Minimum 5 feet — centre 25 minus radius 20. The cosine starts at its own maximum, so the minus sign puts the rider at the BOTTOM at t = 0, which is where a Ferris wheel loads.
widget.lowFeedback: The wheel is not yet 20 feet of swing about a 25-foot centre.
widget.highFeedback: The wheel has passed 20 feet of swing about a 25-foot centre.

explanationVariants: At the top, cos t = −1 and the −20 flips to +20.

widget.prompt: Same wheel. What is the rider's MAXIMUM height, in feet?

commonErrors.feedback: 20 is the RADIUS — the amplitude of the swing, not a height. Top = 25 + 20 = 45.
25 is the axle — the center of the swing. The top sits one radius above: 45.

steps.body: Every part of the formula is a part of the wheel. **Midline = axle height** (the center of the motion). **Amplitude = radius** (how far the rider swings from it). And the entrance: boarding at the BOTTOM means starting at the minimum — exactly what −cos does (it opens at −1).

widget.prompt: For h(t) = 25 − 20 cos t, find the height at t = π (half a rotation), in feet.

commonErrors.feedback: 5 ft is t = 0, the boarding point — half a turn carries the rider all the way to the TOP: 25 − 20(−1) = 45.
25 ft is the QUARTER-turn height (cos = 0, level with the axle). At half a turn cos π = −1: 45 ft.

explanationVariants: −cos opens at its MINIMUM (−cos 0 = −1) — matching a rider who boards at the wheel's bottom.
Plain sine opens at the midline; plain cosine opens at the top. The entrance picks the function.

widget.prompt: Why model the ride with −20 cos t instead of +20 sin t?

options.label: The rider STARTS at the bottom — and −cos starts at its minimum
options.feedback: Right — the function's opening pose must match the physical starting position.

options.label: Sine is wrong because heights can't use sine
options.feedback: Sine works fine for waves — but +20 sin t would open at the MIDLINE (25 ft), and riders board at 5 ft.

options.label: The minus makes the heights negative
options.feedback: The heights stay between 5 and 45 — the minus only flips WHERE the wave starts, not its range.

options.label: Cosine always needs a minus sign
options.feedback: Only bottom-start motion does — a rider boarding at the TOP would take +cos.

steps.body: Any oscillating data fits the same anatomy from last chapter: **midline = (max + min)/2, amplitude = (max − min)/2**. A tide running between 8 ft and 2 ft centers on 5 ft and swings 3 — the wheel's logic, without the wheel.

widget.prompt: A tide oscillates between 8 ft (high) and 2 ft (low). What is the midline of its model, in feet?

commonErrors.feedback: 3 is the AMPLITUDE — the swing (8 − 2)/2. The midline averages: (8 + 2)/2 = 5.
6 is the full high-to-low span — the center is the average of the extremes: 5.

explanationVariants: min = midline − amplitude = 30 − 26 = 4 ft — the boarding platform is the wave's LOWEST point.
In h = 30 − 26 cos t: axle 30, radius 26.

widget.prompt: A ride follows h(t) = 30 − 26 cos t. How high is the boarding platform, in feet?

commonErrors.feedback: 30 is the AXLE — the midline of the swing. Boarding happens a full radius below: 30 − 26 = 4.
56 is the TOP (30 + 26) — riders board at the bottom of the wheel: 4 ft.

hints: Read the formula's anatomy: midline 30, amplitude 26.
−cos opens at the minimum — which is the boarding height.

takeaways: h(t) = (axle) − (radius) cos t models a bottom-boarding wheel.
Midline = axle height, amplitude = radius — formula parts ARE wheel parts.
Any max/min data fits: average for the midline, half-span for the amplitude.
steps.teaser: Next: tides, temperatures, and setting the wave's SPEED from a real period.

concept.body: A smaller wheel, same anatomy. Radius 10, axle 12 ft up: h(t) = 12 − 10 cos t. The lowest point is one radius below the axle — 12 − 10 = 2 ft. Midline from the axle, swing from the radius: the two reads solve every wheel.

explanationVariants: The rider's range is 2 to 22 — centered on the 12 ft axle.

widget.prompt: A wheel of radius 10 ft has its axle 12 ft up. What is the rider's minimum height, in feet?

commonErrors.feedback: 12 is the axle — the CENTER of the swing. The bottom is a radius below it: 2 ft.
22 is the TOP (12 + 10) — the minimum subtracts the radius: 2 ft.
